title: 20-Year Treasury Bond auction (December reopening) — the day's duration-sensitive leg, bidding 90 minutes after the FRN and after the pre-holiday macro block
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Auction-Schedule.pdf), fetched by plain curl 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes) by the treasury-2y-frn-2026-12-23 initial research, text layer inflated stream-by-stream and re-tokenised into 213 auction records. Row reads verbatim `20-Year BOND R / Announcement Thursday, December 17, 2026 / Auction Wednesday, December 23, 2026 / Settlement Monday, December 28, 2026` — the trailing `R` marks it a REOPENING, contrasting with the `20-Year BOND` November row tracked as treasury-20y-bond-2026-11-18. 1:00pm ET is Treasury's standing coupon convention, corroborated mechanically rather than assumed: all 26 20-Year auctions since the tenor's 2020-05-20 revival closed at `01:00 PM` (fiscaldata auctions_query, 4,639-row same-day census since 2014, HTTP 200, 726,093 bytes, pulled this session), and Bonds overall are 260 of 261 at that slot. Filed estimate on the two limits this lane records: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep — the confirming primary is the 2026-12-17 announcement itself. Discovered in the never-assessed initial research of treasury-2y-frn-2026-12-23, 2026-09-09
notes: DISCOVERED during the treasury-2y-frn-2026-12-23 never-assessed initial research (2026-09-09) and proposed because it is not a footnote to that ledger — it is the DIRECT INPUT to that ledger's headline call. The calendar tracks the 20-Year complex at 2026-08-19, 09-15, 10-21, 11-18 and 2027-01-20 and had no row for the December reopening at all. WHY IT EARNS A ROW: the FRN ledger's closing-time result turns on the capacity of Treasury's 11:30 a.m. competitive window, which across 2,227 auction days since 2014 has never held more than two securities (distribution exactly {0: 264, 1: 626, 2: 1337, 3+: zero}). 2026-12-23 carries three auctions — this Bond, the 2-Year FRN reopening, and a 17-Week bill — but this Bond takes the 1:00 p.m. coupon slot, leaving only ONE security in the 11:30 window, which is why the FRN keeps 11:30 a.m. rather than being bumped. If this auction were instead a BILL, that ledger's call would invert. That makes this row a live dependency, not colour. SECOND REASON: it is the day's only duration-sensitive security. 2026-12-23 carries the pre-holiday macro block (PCE confirmed/high, GDP Q3 third, durable goods, new home sales, all 08:30-10:00 ET) and this auction bids at 1:00 p.m., AFTER all of it and after the 11:30 FRN — so the day's close-to-close long-end move is a joint observation of the macro block and this print and cannot be attributed to either alone. THE GRADING CAUTION THE SIBLINGS ALREADY RECORD: treasury-20y-bond-2026-11-18 warns that the reopening yardstick published in treasury-20y-bond-2026-10-21 (a 2.60 bid-to-cover threshold) sits above every 20-Year NEW ISSUE ever printed and must not be carried across slots — this is a REOPENING, so that reopening yardstick is the applicable one and the new-issue grid (floor 2.34, median 2.53, ceiling 2.58, n=15) is not. Neither is re-derived here; this proposal exists to give the auction a calendar row and to record the dependency, and it REGISTERS NOTHING OF ITS OWN — the closing-time prediction that depends on it is FT-treasury-2y-frn-2026-12-23-1, in that event's own fragment. Size, settlement scale and the reopening's own demand read are deliberately left to its initial research. Proposed as an estimate; `symbols: []` and no house playbook is rates-keyed, so nothing here licenses an entry.
